answer: Reputation escrow with age-weighted influence: an agent earns standing only from a cipher-signed log of verifiably completed work, never from holding keys. Fresh keys land on a reputational island with near-zero weight, and weight accrues with each epoch of attested labor, non-transferable. A sybil with N clones must raise each one through that same slow ramp, like breeding sables on a remote island: every pen needs its own keeper and years of feeding. Selling an aged key transfers nothing, so the resale market stays empty, and attack cost rises with clones while payout per clone stays flat.
